en.title: American Airlines' 10 Ex-Alaska Airbus A321neo Jets Keep a Different Seat Map
en.summary: Ten Airbus A321neos American Airlines bought from Alaska Airlines cannot be reconfigured to match the rest of its fleet because they use an older door layout; listed under the same 32Q fleet code, they seat 190 passengers instead of 196 and place exit rows differently.
body: American Airlines operates two versions of the Airbus A321neo that cannot be made identical. Ten aircraft acquired from Alaska Airlines have a different emergency-exit arrangement from the airline's factory-delivered A321neos, a structural feature inherited from their original design. The subfleet traces its origins to Virgin America, which ordered the aircraft before Alaska Airlines acquired the carrier in 2016. Alaska inherited the jets, then retired them as it simplified around Boeing narrowbodies and sold them to American in 2023. Only four of the 10 entered service with Virgin America; the other six joined Alaska directly. The aircraft averaged about 5.6 years old when Alaska retired them, and they began entering American's operation in spring 2024, initially flying from Miami.

The core difference is Airbus Cabin Flex. Early A321neo aircraft were built with a door arrangement broadly resembling the previous-generation A321ceo: four main passenger doors on each side, including an additional pair ahead of the wing. The 10 former Alaska aircraft belong to this earlier configuration. Cabin Flex removed the second pair of full-size doors and introduced modified overwing emergency exits, creating additional usable cabin space and allowing configurations of up to 240 passengers. Their physical structure cannot be converted into the later Cabin Flex arrangement through a normal interior refurbishment. After American's Oasis-style retrofit, each former Alaska A321neo has 190 seats, against 196 in the standard configuration: both have 20 first class seats and 35 Main Cabin Extra seats, but economy is 135 against 141.

Both versions are presented under the same 32Q fleet code, yet the seat maps differ. According to SeatCompare's 2026 guide, the 196-seat A321neo has exit rows at 17 and 27, while the former Alaska aircraft have them at 11 and 24; the last rows are 37 and 36 respectively. The registrations N950XV through N959XV identify the former Alaska group. ch-aviation reported in February 2026 that American operated 75 A321-200NX aircraft alongside the 10 A321-200N jets, with additional standard-range A321neos and XLRs on order.

zh.title: 美國航空10架前阿拉斯加A321neo客機座艙難統一，舊式艙門佈局成限制
zh.summary: 美國航空機隊中有10架自阿拉斯加航空購入的A321neo，因採用舊式艙門佈局而無法改裝為與其餘機隊相同的座艙配置；雖同列32Q機隊代碼，座位數與逃生門位置皆不同，改裝後仍維持190個座位，較標準構型少6個。
body: 美國航空機隊中的10架空中巴士A321neo購自阿拉斯加航空，源自維珍美國航空的訂單。阿拉斯加航空於2016年收購維珍美國航空後承接這批飛機，隨後為簡化機隊而退役並於2023年售予美國航空；其中4架曾在維珍美國航空服役，其餘6架在收購後直接加入阿拉斯加航空。這批飛機退役時平均機齡約5.6年，自2024年春季起由邁阿密開始投入美國航空營運。

關鍵差異在於艙門佈局。這10架飛機屬於較早期的A321neo構型，每側機身有4扇主艙門，包含翼前一對額外艙門；空中巴士其後推出的Cabin Flex設計取消了第二對全尺寸艙門，改用改良的翼上逃生出口，使客艙可用空間增加，配置最高可達240名乘客。由於機身結構無法透過一般客艙改裝轉換為Cabin Flex佈局，美國航空雖以Oasis式客艙整修這批飛機，座位數仍維持190個，頭等艙由16個增至20個，主艙特選座位35個，經濟艙135個；相較之下，標準構型為196個座位，頭等艙20個，主艙特選座位35個，經濟艙141個。
兩種構型同列32Q機隊代碼，但座位圖並不相同。196座構型的逃生門排位於第17排與第27排，前阿拉斯加飛機則在第11排與第24排；最後一排分別為第37排與第36排，洗手間位置也不同。這10架飛機的註冊編號為N950XV至N959XV。ch-aviation於2026年2月報導，美國航空當時營運75架A321-200NX與10架A321-200N，另有標準航程A321neo與XLR訂單待交付。
